name: Connect generation and storage
function: asset management and engineering (customer and generation connections)
summary: Homeowners, businesses and developers apply to connect rooftop solar, battery storage and larger generators to the distribution system. Micro-embedded projects of 10 kW or less get a service layout from a design technologist, and once the ESA has inspected the installation and the agreement is signed a meter technician installs a bidirectional meter within five business days. Larger projects go through a preliminary consultation and a connection impact assessment by the connections engineer, planning and protection staff, sometimes with Hydro One, then an offer to connect and a witnessed commissioning. Most elapsed time is the applicant's installation and decisions; the utility's work is bounded by Distribution System Code deadlines.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario distributor serving about 350,000 customers that does all connection impact assessments in house, with a small connections engineering team inside distribution design.
baseline.notes: 52 micro-embedded connections and 6 CIAs (11.6 MW) in 2021 per the OEB scorecard; process steps follow the Distribution System Code and Hydro Ottawa's DER pages; minutes and waits are estimates.

trigger: A customer, installer or developer submits a micro-embedded generation application or a preliminary consultation request for a larger generator or storage facility.
end_state: The generator is connected and authorized to operate, or the applicant has stopped after the layout, the preliminary consultation or the CIA.

volume.seasonality: Solar applications peak in spring and early summer.

evidence.note: 52 micro-embedded generators connected and 6 CIAs completed in 2021 (scorecard), about 5 a month before counting applications that do not proceed.

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Receive the application and sort it by size
steps.description: A design technologist opens the generation application that arrived by email or the service request form, checks the forms, single-line diagram, meter photos and contractor quote are attached, and sorts it: micro-embedded projects of 10 kW or less go to the service layout path, larger projects to the connections engineer for a preliminary consultation and impact assessment.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: 52 micro-embedded connections and 6 CIAs in 2021 (scorecard); the larger share also counts preliminary consultations that never reach a CIA. Application contents from the Hydro Ottawa DER pages (tier B).

steps.name: Check the single-line diagram and service capacity
steps.description: The technologist checks the inverter rating and certification on the single-line diagram, the main breaker and service size from the photos, and the supplying transformer's loading and existing generation in the GIS, and decides whether a site visit is needed.

error.defect_description: Transformer hosting limit not checked against other generators on it.

evidence.note: Review content from the residential DER page; DSC s.6.2.6 sets different offer times with and without a site assessment. Shares and minutes are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Ask the installer for missing documents
steps.description: The technologist emails the solar installer for a legible single-line diagram, inverter specification sheet or meter base photos and holds the application.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Installer sends the documents
steps.description: The installer sends the missing documents by email, usually after checking with the equipment supplier, and the application returns to review.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess the site
steps.description: The technologist drives to the premise and checks the meter base, the service entrance, the location for the disconnect switch and the route of the generator wiring, and photographs the existing service.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Site assessment option and its longer layout time on the residential DER page; minutes include travel and are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue the service layout and connection requirements
steps.description: The technologist drafts the service layout for the generator: metering arrangement (bidirectional meter), disconnect location, whether the service must be isolated, connection fee, and the connection agreement to sign, and emails it to the customer and installer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.6.2.6: offer to connect a micro-embedded generator within 15, 30 or 60 days

evidence.note: Layout within 15 days without and 60 days with a site assessment, valid 90 days (residential DER page); DSC s.6.2.6 offer timelines and at least 30 days to accept.

steps.name: Customer pays, installs the system and passes ESA inspection
steps.description: The customer pays the connection fee, the installer mounts the panels or battery and wires the inverter, the ESA inspects and issues its authorization, and the customer signs the connection agreement. Many projects wait for equipment deliveries or incentive approvals.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Conditions listed in DSC s.6.2.7 and the residential DER page; durations and drop-out share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Verify the conditions and raise the work and meter orders
steps.description: The technologist checks the ESA authorization and the signed agreement against the layout, confirms payment, and raises a meter order for the bidirectional meter and, when the service must be isolated, a work order for a line crew. The five-business-day connection clock starts here.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.6.2.7 and Ontario Regulation 22/04: ESA authorization, connection agreement and payment before connecting a micro-embedded generator

evidence.note: DSC s.6.2.7 conditions and the 5-business-day standard met for all 52 micro connections in 2021 (scorecard).

steps.name: Install the bidirectional meter and energize
steps.description: A meter technician drives to the premise, removes the existing meter, installs and programs a bidirectional smart meter, closes the generator disconnect with the installer present, confirms export is registered and records the meter change. About a quarter of jobs also need a line crew to isolate the service, arranged through crew scheduling.

error.defect_description: Meter programmed without the export channel, so generation credits are missed.

evidence.note: Meter work and energization by the utility (residential DER page) within 5 business days (DSC s.6.2.7); minutes include travel and are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the application and set up net metering billing
steps.description: The technologist closes the application, confirms the meter change reached the customer system and asks billing to set up the net metering or load displacement billing arrangement.

error.defect_description: Billing arrangement not set up and credits missed.

evidence.note: Net metering billing under O. Reg. 541/05 (Conditions of Service s.3.4.1); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the preliminary consultation report
steps.description: The connections engineer reviews the preliminary consultation request for a larger project, looks up the feeder, station capacity, short-circuit levels and existing generation, and sends the applicant a report on feasibility and likely requirements.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.6.2.9.1: respond to a preliminary consultation within 15 days

evidence.note: Report within 15 days (business DER page; DSC s.6.2.9.1); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Applicant decides and submits the CIA application
steps.description: The applicant decides whether to pursue the project and, if so, submits the connection impact assessment application with engineer-stamped drawings and the CIA fee.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: CIA application with stamped drawings and fee (business DER page; Conditions of Service s.3.4.2); share proceeding and durations are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Check the CIA application and notify the transmitter
steps.description: The engineer checks the application and drawings are complete, deems it complete or asks for corrections, and where the project affects the transmission connection files a request with Hydro One within 15 days.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.6.2.14A: file with the transmitter or host distributor within 15 days

evidence.note: Transmitter filing within 15 days (DSC s.6.2.14A); Hydro Ottawa consults Hydro One on the customer's behalf (Conditions of Service s.3.4.2).

steps.name: Run load flow, voltage and fault studies
steps.description: A system planning engineer models the generator on the feeder and checks voltage rise, thermal loading, fault current contribution and the station's reverse power limits, and lists any line or equipment upgrades.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Impact assessment contents in DSC s.6.2.14; all CIA work done internally (scorecard). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review protection and transfer trip requirements
steps.description: A protection and control technologist reviews the generator's interconnection protection, anti-islanding and the need for transfer trip or a recloser, against the utility's generation technical guideline. The work runs alongside the planning study.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Protection requirements per the generation technical guideline (Conditions of Service s.3.4); DSC s.6.2.14 includes protection impacts. Share needing Hydro One review is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hydro One completes its review
steps.description: Hydro One reviews the effect of the generator on its transformer station and transmission protection and returns its comments or requirements, which the distributor cannot speed up.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Host review extends the CIA timeline by 15 days (DSC s.6.2.12-6.2.13); durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the CIA report
steps.description: The connections engineer combines the study, protection requirements and any transmitter comments into the CIA report: feasibility, voltage and fault impacts, required upgrades, metering and protection, and an estimate range.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: CIA contents in DSC s.6.2.14; hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and sign the CIA
steps.description: The engineering manager reviews the report and its assumptions and signs it as the professional engineer of record, or returns it for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Professional Engineers Act (Ontario): engineering reports sealed by a licensed professional engineer

evidence.note: Author's estimate; engineering reports are signed by a licensed engineer in Ontario.

steps.name: Issue the CIA to the applicant and Hydro One
steps.description: The engineer sends the signed CIA to the applicant and, where involved, to Hydro One, and records the date for the on-time measure.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.6.2.12-6.2.13: CIA within 60 to 105 days

evidence.note: 6 CIAs in 2021 completed within 60 to 90 days (scorecard; DSC s.6.2.12-6.2.13).

steps.name: Applicant decides to proceed
steps.description: The applicant decides within the CIA's six-month validity whether to proceed, agrees the project scope and pays for the detailed cost estimate.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: CIA expires after six months (business DER page); detailed estimate paid for before the offer (DSC s.6.2.16). Share proceeding is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the offer to connect and connection cost agreement
steps.description: The technologist designs the utility-side work (metering, recloser or transfer trip, line upgrades) and the engineer prices it into the detailed cost estimate, offer to connect and connection cost agreement.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.6.2.16 and 6.2.18: detailed cost estimate and offer within 90 days; connection cost agreement

evidence.note: Offer within 90 days of payment (DSC s.6.2.16); connection cost agreement (DSC s.6.2.18; Conditions of Service s.3.4.2). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Applicant signs, pays and builds the facility
steps.description: The applicant signs the offer and agreement, pays, builds the generation or storage facility and has it inspected by the ESA; Hydro Ottawa holds a pre-construction meeting.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Signed offer, payment, pre-construction meeting and ESA authorization on the business DER page; duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Raise the work and meter orders for the utility-side work
steps.description: The technologist raises the capital work order for the recloser, transfer trip or line work and the meter order for the generation metering, and releases them to crew scheduling and metering.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; hand-offs follow the organisation file's process map.

steps.name: Witness the commissioning tests
steps.description: A protection and control technologist drives to the site and witnesses the applicant's commissioning tests against the commissioning plan: protection trips, anti-islanding, transfer trip and metering, and signs the test record.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Hydro Ottawa DER commissioning guide (ECG0024): utility witness of protection and anti-islanding tests before parallel operation

evidence.note: Utility witness of commissioning under its commissioning guide (business DER page); hours include travel and are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check settings and paperwork during commissioning
steps.description: The connections engineer attends the same commissioning, checks the as-built single-line diagram and settings against the CIA and agreement, and confirms the ESA authorization and agreements are signed.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Generation starts after commissioning passes and all agreements are signed (business DER page); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Authorize generation and notify operations and billing
steps.description: The engineer issues the authorization to operate in parallel, tells the control room to add the generator to the operating diagram and asks billing and settlement to set up the generator account.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Authorization to operate in parallel issued only after commissioning and signed agreements

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the close-out.

exceptions.name: Missing or unclear documents
exceptions.description: The single-line diagram or meter photos are missing or illegible; the application waits for the installer.

exceptions.name: Micro project abandoned
exceptions.description: The customer does not install within the layout's validity or cancels.

exceptions.name: Transmitter review
exceptions.description: The generator affects the Hydro One station; the CIA waits for the transmitter's comments.

exceptions.name: Larger project stops after consultation or CIA
exceptions.description: Applicants test feasibility and stop when upgrade costs or capacity limits appear.

benchmarks.unit: share of CIAs within 60 to 90 days, 2021
calendar days from application to connection or stop

evidence.note: Author's estimate: micro layouts in 15 to 60 days (residential DER page) plus one to five months of customer installation and five business days to connect; larger projects take 6 to 18 months but are about one case in seven, and half of them stop after the consultation.

pain_points.description: Incomplete micro applications from installers and illegible single-line diagrams cause back-and-forth.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: A few engineers do all CIA studies in house, so a cluster of larger applications competes with developer work for the same people.

evidence.note: All CIA work done internally (scorecard).

pain_points.description: Transmitter reviews add weeks that the distributor does not control.

evidence.note: Separate timelines when a host or transmitter CIA is needed (DSC s.6.2.12-6.2.13).

pain_points.description: Bidirectional meter installs must fit within five business days alongside other meter work.

assumptions: Micro projects are 86% of applications: 52 connections and 6 CIAs in 2021, plus preliminary consultations that never become CIAs.
The 2019-2022 micro threshold was 10 kW (scorecard); Hydro Ottawa's current pages use 12 kW and the 2022 DER Connection Procedures, so the forms differ slightly from those in the reference period.

Meter technicians, protection and control technologists and the engineering manager take part although the organisation file's process map lists only connections engineers, design technologists and planning engineers.
A micro layout is recorded as a connection offer to the applicant, an object the organisation file's process map does not list as an output of this process.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's rates (wage x 1.40). FTEs add 20% to hands-on time.
The Distribution System Code cited is the August 2026 revision; sections 6.2.7, 6.2.12 and 6.2.13 match the 60 to 90 day and five-business-day standards reported for 2021 in the OEB scorecard.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa Conditions of Service, ECS0012 Rev. 8 (proposed, effective December 2021)
sources.supports: s.2.1: design and material prepayments, deposits before field work; s.2.1.3: offer to connect contents, economic evaluation, expansion deposit (letter of credit, cash, surety), alternative bid with qualified contractors and 2-year warranty; s.2.1.5: ESA Connection Authorization Certificate required before energizing and must match address, voltage and ampacity; duct banks inspected before concrete and before backfill with a mandrel test, pads and vaults inspected before equipment; s.2.1.7: Installation and Service Agreement for developers; s.3.1.2: subdivision site information (plan, grading, phasing, load summary); s.3.1.3: utility designates supply point and meter base location, installs up to 30 m of service conductor, inspects service entry to the meter base; s.3.4: DER Form B, CIA fee, Installation and Service Agreement with Connection Cost Agreement, Hydro One consulted on the customer's behalf; Appendix G: quotes expire after 90 days, one free customer layout per property per year, two-person line crew isolations.

sources.title: Business DER connection process
sources.supports: Larger DER: preliminary consultation report within 15 days; CIA application with P.Eng-stamped drawings and fee; CIA at least 60 days (simplified CIA 30 days), expires after six months; project manager assigned after intent to proceed; offer to connect signed and paid; pre-construction meeting; commissioning plan and Hydro Ottawa witness of commissioning; ESA connection authorization; CIA fees $1,000 (small) to $5,700 (large).

sources.title: DER connection process (residential)
sources.supports: Micro-DER: application with single-line diagram, meter photos and Micro-DER form; service layout within 15 days without and 60 days with a site assessment, valid 90 days; contractor installs, ESA inspects and certifies; customer signs the micro-generation connection agreement; Hydro Ottawa does meter work (bidirectional meter) and energizes; connection fee about $500, about $1,200 when isolation is needed.

sources.title: Distribution System Code (last revised August 1, 2026)
sources.supports: s.6.1.1: respond to a written connection request within 15 calendar days and make an offer to connect within 60 calendar days; s.3.2 and Appendix B: economic evaluation, capital contribution, expansion deposit, alternative bid and final economic evaluation after energization; s.6.2.6: micro-embedded offer within 15, 30 or 60 days and at least 30 days to accept; s.6.2.7: connect a micro-embedded generator within 5 business days of ESA authorization, agreement and payment (90% of the time); s.6.2.9.1: preliminary consultation response within 15 days; s.6.2.12 and 6.2.13: CIA within 60, 75, 90 or 105 days; s.6.2.14A: file with the transmitter within 15 days; s.6.2.16: detailed cost estimate and offer to connect within 90 days of payment.

sources.title: Scorecard - Hydro Ottawa Limited (2017-2021) and 2021 Scorecard Management Discussion and Analysis
sources.supports: 5,024 new residential and small business services connected in 2021, 100% within five business days of conditions being met or as scheduled with the customer (DSC s.7.2, 90% minimum); 9,001 appointments for service upgrades, meter checks and service layouts in 2021 (98.86% on time, four-hour window under DSC s.7.4); missed appointments mainly caused by emergencies and weather; 6 CIAs totalling 11,635.8 kW in 2021 all on time, timelines 60 to 90 days, all CIA work done internally; 52 micro-embedded generators (10 kW or less) connected in 2021, 100% within five business days.
